name: ssrf-battery probe corpus
notes: Declarative: every probe below is generated from target x encoding, no free-text
payloads. Placeholders are expanded by probespec.py; every IPv6 form is
rendered through stdlib canonical compression ([64:ff9b::7f00:1], not
ideographic full stops for dots, {PATH} the request path (default '/').
parse = what ipaddress.ip_address() sees in the host: ip_literal means the
host IS a literal IP; name means it is hostname-shaped (resolution-dependent).

targets.rationale: Canonical loopback; every guard blocks the plain form, encodings are the test.
RFC1918 private space; the NAT64 form 64:ff9b::a00:1 appeared in published SSRF-guard test suites.
AWS/GCP/Azure metadata endpoint; 64:ff9b::a9fe:a9fe is the published NAT64 form of it.
Azure Wire Server; published SSRF guards block it explicitly, so its encodings are a fair probe.
v6 loopback in canonical and exploded forms.
GCP dual-stack metadata endpoint in fd00::/8 ULA space.

encodings.rationale: RFC 6052 well-known NAT64 prefix 64:ff9b::/96 with the internal v4 in the low 32 bits. IANA marks the prefix globally routable, so ipaddress.is_global returns True and is_global-default-deny guards (the pydantic-ai class) and manually maintained CIDR lists (ToolHive, Roundcube, MCP fetch) pass it. On NAT64/DNS64 egress it translates back to the internal v4.
RFC 8215 local-use NAT64 prefix 64:ff9b:1::/48. ip-address CVE-2026-101910 exists because no classifier recognized this range; pydantic-ai's advisory calls it out alongside the well-known prefix.
IPv4-mapped IPv6 with dotted v4 tail. Guards that only ipaddress-check v6 nets (fd00::/8 etc.) miss it; Python exposes .ipv4_mapped but a net-list check without unwrapping does not use it.
IPv4-mapped IPv6, pure hex form (::ffff:7f00:1). Same class as the dotted form; string blocklists that match '127.0.0.1' miss it.

Deprecated IPv4-compatible IPv6 (::7f00:1). pydantic-ai's advisory covers IPv4-compatible addresses; most resolvers treat it as plain v6, where the low 32 bits still route to the v4 on dual stacks. Flagged conditional because modern kernels differ.

6to4 transition encoding 2002:<v4>:: (2002:7f00:1:: embeds 127.0.0.1). Named in the isPublicIP/transition-encodings advisory class alongside NAT64; needs a 6to4 relay to actually terminate, hence conditional.

Teredo 2001::/32 with the obfuscated client v4 (XOR 0xffffffff; 127.0.0.1 -> 80ff:fffe) in the low 32 bits. Rarest of the transition encodings; carried for completeness of the transition-encoding class.
Classic dword integer form (2130706433). ipaddress rejects it so IP-literal guards see a hostname, but POSIX inet_aton/getaddrinfo accept it as 127.0.0.1.
Hex dword form (0x7f000001); same inet_aton semantics as the decimal dword.
Octal dotted form (0177.0000.0000.0001); inet_aton family treats leading-0 groups as octal, ipaddress rejects.
Hex dotted form (0x7f.0x0.0x0.0x1); curl and inet_aton accept, ipaddress rejects.
Short form (127.1 = 127.0.0.1); the classic a.b/c compression inet_aton honors.

Circled digits (①②⑦.⓪.⓪.①): Unicode best-fit maps U+2460-series digits to ASCII digits before resolution, so WHATWG-URL/IDNA resolvers reach 127.0.0.1 while the guard sees a foreign hostname. Established by the curl best-fit HackerOne report and url-parse #241; the MCP fetch IDNA advisory is the check-vs-connect differential.
Fullwidth digits (１２７．０．０．１): same best-fit normalization family as circled digits.
ASCII digits with ideographic full stops (127。0。0。1): separator normalization, the exact shape of the curl best-fit report.

Exploded zero-padded form (0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1). Guards doing string matching on '::1' or net membership both handle it when they parse; carried as the v6-canonical control encoding that a competent guard must hold.
Canonical short form (::1, fd00:ec2::254); the v6 equivalent of the plain-IPv4 control.
Userinfo trick: allowlist checks that substring-match the trusted domain see safe.example, the real host is the internal IP. urlsplit-based guards see through it; string-contains guards do not.
Backslash + @: WHATWG parsers treat the backslash as a path separator so the real host is the IP; lax splits see safe.example as the host. Parser-differential class (Claroty confusion family).

controls.rationale: A guard that rejects everything must not be scored as holding the line.
Public IP literal the guard must accept.
Plaintext internal literal the guard must reject; establishes the guard exists at all.
